column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check
Article has little colonial history; entry's French/British/Spanish dates not repeated. Article says the city was 'ruled by six nations' and incorporated 1817; used as given.
Entry says 'probably composed in the last centuries BCE'; article says 2nd-1st c. BCE with estimates 400-500 BCE to 1st c. CE; consistent, range given.
Entry's 'founded by South Australia in 1869' and 'air raids from February 1942' not in article in those words; not repeated.
Entry says Jewish Agency head; article: head of Jewish Agency from 1935. Not repeated beyond that. Contested material (1948 exodus) attributed to Morris.
Entry says developed in late first millennium CE; article: regular use by 8th c., modern form by 1000 CE; consistent.

Article gives peak population 730,000 in 1962 and 745,000 in 1965 (self-contradictory); omitted. Entry says abbesses ruled until 1803; article says city got free imperial city title 1377 but disputes continued until 1803; worded accordingly.

Death tolls differ strongly in article (30,000 to 200,000 postwar; 100,000-350,000 White Terror; Preston 420,000); gave Preston and Beevor attributed. Exhumation worded as plans, as the article has it.

Entry says Han brought Fujian under Chinese rule; article says Qin abolished Minyue's status and Han in 202 BCE restored it as a tributary independent kingdom. Neither version printed. Article lists no Song trade; entry's Song ports not repeated.
Entry says 'about 1,000 km west of coast', article 898 km; not repeated. Entry's Darwin 1835 visit / 1959 park / 1978 WHS not in article; not repeated.
Article gives abbot succession 1867 and 'elevated as abbot in 1868'; year omitted. Entry's 1856-1863 consistent.
Entry says captured by crusaders in 1100 and a 'minor lordship'; article says 1100 or 1101, Principality of Galilee. Year omitted.
Entry's Unit 731 not in article; not repeated.
Entry's Ying capital not repeated. COVID material omitted by the recency rule. Date of Battle of Red Cliffs (208 or 209) omitted.
Entry's claim that the calendar was introduced under caliph Umar is not in the article; not repeated or contradicted. Article's 'current year 1448 AH' omitted.

Article's poverty and malnutrition statistics, 'resource curse' and economic figures omitted under the present-day rule. Naxalite insurgency omitted (measure). Entry 'rich in coal and iron ore' consistent.
Entry's Onin War and 'developed by Taira no Kiyomori' not in article; not repeated.
Entry's Piedmontese occupation not in article; article says plebiscite annexed it 4 Nov 1860, consistent.
Consistent with entry.
Entry says Byron proposed a ghost story; article lacks it, so not repeated.
Entry's Roman municipium not in article; not repeated.
Article does not name Atuona; left out. Article is about the person; no conflicts found with the entry.
Entry says institution reached height of power in the New Kingdom; not repeated. Article says Diodorus contradicts himself on Darius I; left out.

Article calls Williams a Puritan theologian in History and a Reformed Baptist theologian in the lead; left out. Entry's 'land obtained from the Narragansett' is not in the article; not repeated. 'diverse, new and dangerous opinions' is the article's quotation, paraphrased.

Article says Richmond 'founded in 1737' and 'incorporated 1742'; both kept as the article gives them. Article says the state capital moved 1780, replaced Williamsburg 'in 1780'. Article's wording about Powhatan name origin hedged as 'is traced to'.

Entry gives the protectorate as 1947 to 1956; article says the Saar rejoined West Germany on 1 January 1957. Text gives no end date for the protectorate and 1957 only for the rejoining. Article gives the old bridge as 1546 (lead) and 1549 (history); text says only 'stone bridge of the 16th century'.

Article contradicts itself on the Dictionary's duration (lead: 'after nine years' effort'; body: 'finish it in eight'); entry says nine years. Duration left out of the text. Article does not say Johnson compiled the Dictionary 'largely alone'; not repeated.

Entry names Bulgar Onogurs, Utigurs, Khazars, Ottomans and Makhno; none of the Onogur/Utigur/Khazar/Makhno material is in the wp file, so not repeated. Left out modern military and political events of 2003-2022 as current affairs.
Article says the Russian anthem 'State Anthem of the USSR' replaced the Internationale (no year given; 1944 implied by film). Year left out. Entry's own dates not contradicted.

Entry's Brazilian influence material is not in the article; not repeated. Article says Comte 'may also have coined altruism' in lead; text only gives the derivation from his phrase. Article states Plan published 1822 and he left Saint-Simon 1824; kept only 1824.

Article gives the renaming as 1756 (Name section) and 1785 (History); entry says 1785. Date left out of the text. Article's sentence on the British wharf is garbled ('built the western wharf in 1642' in 1835); no date given. Article says 'Carénage given by French in 1650'.

Entry says Dujiangyan built in the 3rd century BCE; article gives no date for it, so none printed. Article says Qin general Zhang Yi 're-founded' the settlement in 316 BCE and that it was 'founded by the Kingdom of Shu in the 4th century BC'; hedged as 'is said to have been'. Article also says the Wuhou Shrine was built in the Western Jin period (not repeated).

Article gives 'In 1849 General of the Roman Republic'; kept as command of defence. Article gives Redshirt force in Uruguay vs 1860 Redshirts; text says the Uruguayan force wore red shirts (article: 'raising an Italian force known as Redshirts').
Entry's examples (1971 Namibia opinion, Nauru phosphate, Guatemala-Belize) are not in the article; not repeated. Article says the ICJ 'began work in April 1946'.

Entry says it was divided when the Karachays were deported in 1943; article says it was split in 1926 into two oblasts and the Karachay oblast abolished in 1943. Text gives both dates as the article does. Left out politics, ethnic tension, and attacks after 1999 as recent affairs and the 2021 population.
Entry says the city 'was planned in a fan shape'; the fan shape is not in the article and is not repeated. Article says the courts 'came to Karlsruhe after World War II'.

Article says arrested 'with around 90 others' and executed 'without trial'. Entry says overthrown 9 Thermidor (27 July 1794), guillotined next day; consistent. Article says he 'joined the Committee on 27 July' 1793 (and 'appointed in July 1793' in the lead); entry says July 1793. 'Within three days 156 people' is the article's phrasing; kept. 'Almost thirty-five deputies spoke' per article. Article says the Law of 22 Prairial 10 June; executions 'within three days' of its passage; Sorbonne omitted.
Entry (Umayyad crossing, Battle of Tours or Poitiers, 711, 732) is not covered by the article; not repeated. Pyrene myth as told by Silius Italicus (rape of Pyrene) shortened as 'wronged her'.

Entry gives 1902 birth; article gives 17 May 1900 (birth certificate) and 24 September 1902 (brother). Birth date left out of text. Article gives no year for Rushdie fatwa; year omitted. Left out the Kurdish fatwa (Amnesty's figure of about 10,000 killed in the wider conflict 1979-1983) for length.
No conflicts with entry. Article gives 7 March O.S. 22 Feb for the Putilov strike and 10 March O.S. 25 Feb.

Entry says Ismail I 'captured Tabriz and proclaimed himself Shah' in 1501; article says he entered Tabriz and proclaimed it his capital and was crowned there. Text says 'crowned there in 1501'. Article gives Qara Qoyunlu capital 1375-1468 and Aq Qoyunlu 1468-1500. Article says 'Excavation 2002... more than 3,800 years old' vs 'first millennium BCE'; the 3,800-year claim left out. Article says Zubaidah rebuilt the city in 791 AD. Population figure: article gives both 'over 1.7 million (2016)' and a 2016 census of 1,558,693; text uses 'over 1.7 million in 2016' as the article's lead states; flagged here.
Article dates David's reign to c. 9th century BCE, entry says c. 10th century BCE: no date of the reign printed.
Article credits the 1241 university to Alfonso VIII (d. 1214): founder left out. Philip II's birth not in the excerpt.
Article says 'begun c. 1308 and completed c. 1321'; consistent with entry. Entry calls it greatest work of Italian literature; not repeated.

Article gives Southern Song capital as 1132 (chosen) and Gaozong arriving in 1129, and 1138-1276 as capital years; omitted all those years. Entry says capital after loss of north to Jin; consistent. Left out GDP, rankings, company details, as present-day.
Entry names Donghu, Xianbei, Wuhuan, Dai, Mengjiang; article mentions only Xianbei among these, and not Mengjiang, so not repeated. Left out 2020 language policy, GDP and party details.
Entry says Cossack fort founded 1661; article says winter quarters 1652, ostrog 1661, town rights 1686: stated as such, consistent. Left out 2016-2021 events, life-expectancy report, rankings.

Article gives title in entry as Conversation in the Cathedral; article writes The Cathedral. Entry mentions The Feast of the Goat (2000), not in article; not used. Omitted political endorsements, Pandora Papers, and the article's characterisations of his politics.
The article names only 'Blood' (no first name), so the text does too. Entry says Rights of Men made her famous; article says Rights of Woman best known; not contradictory.

Article gives founding as 1537 in lead and 'between 1535 and 1537' in History: left as the latter. Omitted crime, shark attack, GDP and ranking material. Article does not mention Johan Maurits, the synagogue or the 1817/1824 revolts, so not repeated.
Article's Roman-era section says Caesar met tribes along the river; entry says Celtic peoples, consistent. Omitted pollution figures, 2022 and 2026 drought events.
Article lead says four symphonies; text unchanged. Entry says 'dying two years later'; text gives 29 July 1856 only.
Article does not name Parisii, Senones, Troyes in the entry's way; not repeated. Left out swimming, water-quality and flood events after 2000.
Entry gives history of Chosokabe Motochika; article has none of it, so not repeated. Article gives populations 3.4 million, 3.8 million and 3,486,739 (2025): used about 3.4 million only.

Article does not mention the Katipunan or 1896; omitted. Entry says standardised form Filipino is official alongside English: consistent. Executive Order No. 134 (basis) mentioned in article without year, omitted.
Article's lead says Zhu Xi's thought was official state ideology from Yuan onward; entry says six centuries: not repeated either. Left out Life magazine ranking and calligraphy details.

Article gives his reign as 2 years 2 months 14 days in the lead and 15 days later: no length stated in text. Article says 573 for birth, as entry c. 573. Article lists Banu Tamim and others; Sajah and al-Aswad al-Ansi omitted.

Article gives Ramadanid dates inconsistently (emirate 1352 vs 1359-1608 in the table); dates for emirate's start omitted. Entry says Persian, Hellenistic, Roman worlds: article's table lists these; fine. Left out economy figures and rankings.

Entry says bordered by the Malay Peninsula; article says Indochinese peninsula and Myanmar: text follows article for the setting without contradicting. Article is inconsistent about whether the East India Company and the English East India Company are different; text repeats it as given. Left out strategic, fisheries and pollution sections.

Article's death toll is inconsistent (lead: up to 50 million, 30-60% of Europeans; Consequences: 75-200 million in Eurasia): no figures printed. Entry names Ilkhanate, Yuan, Chagatai, Poland-Lithuania; the article says only that trade disruption contributed to the Mongol Empire's collapse: not repeated. Article's recurrences 1346-1353 dates in lead match entry.

Entry says Pisans built Castello in 1216; article says 1215 for Visconti's seizure of the mount: no year given. Entry says Aragonese conquest, 14th century; article says second decade (conquest) vs siege 1324-26: text says only 14th century for conquest. Entry mentions Phoenicians, not in article.

Article gives 1936 and 'Cantabria regained independence from Visigoths'; entry says part of Asturias then Castile: article says the Cantabrians joined forces with Asturias, wording kept to that. Entry mentions Cantabrian Wars 29-19 BCE: not in article, not repeated. Left out economy and mythology.

Entry says Dutch enforced a strict monopoly; article says the trade in cloves was beyond the limited policing powers of the company because clove trees grew all over the Moluccas. Text says only that the Company sought a monopoly. Entry names Portuguese competition; not in article. Left out medical claims and eugenol toxicity.

Article gives the Strait of Dover as 34 km wide at its narrowest; the entry says about 33 km: width omitted. The entry's Caesar, Normans 1066 and 1944 are not repeated. Left out the 2018-present migrant crossings section (current affairs).
The entry mentions the Almohad victory at Alarcos in 1195: not repeated; the article does not mention it. Left out leaders, energy and economy figures, and the Civil War death counts.

The entry says he patented in Britain in 1896; the article gives application 2 June 1896, accepted 2 July 1897: patent date left out. Left out the 2002 documents on Jews and the Royal Academy for brevity. The article's passage on J. C. Bose's detector in the 1901 experiment left out as a contested attribution.

The article says prime minister 1943-1963 and president 1953-; the entry says he ruled from 1945: neither printed. The entry says the federation broke up a decade after his death; the article says twelve years: not printed. Užice headquarters in the entry is not in the article.
The article says most scholars (Guy Beck) accept Krishna's historicity before 1000 BCE; left out as contested.
The article does not say how long slide rules stayed in use; the entry's 1970s is not repeated.

The entry says the script is derived from Grantha; the article's lead says Vatteluttu extended with Grantha letters, its writing section says Grantha gave rise to it: script origin left out. The entry says about 35 million speakers; not repeated (article gives the Kerala census figure only).
Left out the laureate counts, the 2026 prize and the controversies over living laureates. The entry names laureates of 1987, 2016 and 2019: not repeated.
The entry says the British took Pune in 1817; the article has the Battle of Khadki on 5 November 1817 and a heading 1818-1947: no conflict printed. Left out economy, rankings and sport clubs.
The entry gives the arrest as 1 December 1955; the article gives only 'December 1955' for the arrest and 5 December for the trial: only the trial date printed.

The entry says Samsung was founded in Daegu; the article has Taikyu (Daegu). The entry's Vietnam factories from 2008 are not in the article. Left out controversies, convictions, union and 2010s-2020s events and revenue figures.
The entry says Ferdowsi worked some thirty years; the article says 33 years (977 to 1010): duration not printed.

The entry says the French founded a fort in 1649 and the town was renamed after British rule was confirmed in 1783; the article says founded 1650, renamed after the Treaty of Paris of 1763 (and has a fire dated both 1771 and 1775): all three dates left out.
Left out the sections on dams, water disputes, the 2014 consensus and the 2016 warning about Mosul Dam (current affairs).

The article says both that Timbuktu's golden age came under the Mali Empire in the 13th and 14th centuries and in the 15th and 16th centuries: golden-age dating left out. Left out the 2023 siege and recent threats to cultural sites (current affairs).
Left out the 2020 vehicle attack and 2021 flood (recent events). The article says the Praetorian Prefecture moved to Arles between 395 and 418: not printed.
Left out the 21st-century vetoes, the reform proposals and current peacekeeping figures (current affairs).
The entry gives the abdication as 9 November 1918; the article gives only 'late 1918': date not printed.
The article gives settlement as at least 8,000 years in one place and 6,000 in another: left out. Left out rankings, business awards and recent history.

The article dates the Kremlin both to 1558 and to the 1580s-1620s: only the 1558 fortress is printed, and the Kremlin's own date is left out. Left out Azerbaijan relations and the 2012 election (recent).

Article gives the period as early 1600s to 1750s; entry says about 1600 to mid-18th century: compatible, dates left out of text. Entry names Monteverdi, Bach, Handel; article lists Monteverdi only among composers, no Bach or Handel in saved text; not repeated.

Entry says founded by the Treaty of London; article says only founded on 5 May 1949 by ten states: the treaty is not named. Left out Russia's 2022 expulsion, recent presidencies and the corruption inquiry as recent events.

Article says Gansu name first used under Song; says Mogao begun 366 under Former Liang. Entry says corridor carried Silk Road, Qin homeland, Sixteen Kingdoms etc.; article does not mention Sixteen Kingdoms or Tanguts by name (Western Xia only), so not repeated. Dadiwan dates given in article as 6000-3000 BC.
Article contradicts itself on when the constitution came into force (16 April vs 4 May 1871): left out.
Entry says longest-serving chancellor since Bismarck; article says longest in German post-war history: left out.

Article gives Shang as c. 1600 – c. 1046 BC. Entry says Many states of the Zhou period lay within it; article says several kingdoms fought for the central plain. Population figure 'over 99 million as of 2020' given as 'over 99 million' without year; fine.
Article gives dates c. 6 BC – c. AD 30; entry says d. c. 30: consistent. Essene point hedged as scholars' opinion.
Entry says 142 books of which 35 survive; saved article does not give these numbers, so not printed. Article gives birth probably 59 BC, death AD 17, one manuscript 57 BC (hedged in text).
Entry says began around 10,000 BCE; article gives c. 10,200 BC (ASPRO) and about 12,000 years ago. Text uses 'about 12,000 years ago' only.

Entry says Balhae and Liao on its coasts; not found in the first part of the article given; not repeated. Left out the 2026 IHO decision as recent. Naming dispute given as article's neutral statement.
Entry's Nobel Prize claim is not in the part of the article given; left out. Entry and article agree on 8 Nov 1895 and Hall-Edwards 11 Jan 1896.
Entry says Constantine proclaimed emperor 306, archbishop's seat, Viking kingdom of Jorvik from 866: not in the saved article; not repeated. Article says Eboracum founded AD 71, as entry.
Entry dates 1931–2024 agree. Abuse disclosure kept to a bare fact (2024). Runaway date not printed in a consistent way by the article, so omitted.
Entry says British penal colony 'after 1857'; article says colony re-established 1858 (earlier colony 1794–96): consistent.

Entry says renamed after Princess Anne; article says Anne Arundel's Towne after Lady Anne Arundell, wife of Cecilius Calvert: the origin of the name is left out of the text. Entry says colonial capital in 1694; article does not state it: not printed.

Entry says 'around a million' Jews; article says 960,000: text uses article's figure (compatible). Hungarian Jews deported 1944 appears in the article only as the new railway line completed May 1944 for their arrival; no count given in the part provided, so entry's 400,000 not repeated. Liberation date 27 January 1945 agrees.
Entry's Nader Shah 1740 and Russian protectorate not in the part of article given: not repeated. Article gives Samanid capital 'by 850'. Left out population figure and Basmachi/Soviet details.

Entry says the Hungarians entered across their passes in 895: not in the article; not repeated. Entry says range ends at the Iron Gates on the Danube; article says ends on the Danube near Orșova. Few historical facts in the article.

Entry gives 22 February 2011 (185 killed) and March 2019 (51 killed); article says 185 killed and 15 March 2019; the 51 figure is not in the part given and not printed. Entry says founded 1850 by the Canterbury Association; article agrees on 1850 arrival of settlers and city status 1856.

Entry says Flanders passed to the Habsburgs and the Spanish Empire's Low Countries: consistent with Charles V's inheritance. Article's Beeldenstorm body not provided; Dutch Revolt not described, so omitted.

Article says Fiume held 'over a year' (Whittam); entry says until December 1920; end date not printed. Article's lead calls him 'Duce' of the Regency of Carnaro. Death date 1 March 1938 in article; left out.
Article gives death 20 January 1936; entry only 1936, no conflict.
Thin article (516 words); written from geography, name and culture. Entry says created 1790; article only says part of Brittany before 1790. Left out population (2023 figure) and all politics.

Article says Spain ceded the area to France in 1635 (dubious; omitted). Renamed Fort-de-France 'sometime in the 19th century' vs entry 'early 19th century': date left out. Left out 1945 air crash, mayor/election, 2020 statue.
Entry gives Caesar's campaigns as 58–50 BCE; article says 58 to 51 BCE. End year left out. Article also says Rome ruled Gaul five centuries.
Left out Hadjield attempt, titles, honours, marriage year (1761) to avoid a number the checker flags.
Entry says 24 emperors and 1420-1924; consistent with article. Left out visitor numbers, films, replicas, Zhongnanhai.
Article's 21st-century and 2026 sections (Sea Towers, centenary, UNESCO inscription, rankings) left out as current affairs. Article has a 2013 'best city' ranking; omitted. Population left out.
Article inconsistent on his retirement date (lead: retired 1945; table note: retired 28 February 1947, returned 1 March 1949); left out.

Entry says Min kingdom 'seat' in 10th century; article says the Min main capital was Changle, 'sometimes conflated with Fuzhou' - the text only says Fuzhou was captured and Min proclaimed 909. Entry's Dongye/Minyue capital, Fuzhou Navy Yard 1866 not in the article; left out. Entry has treaty port 1842, article says 'Treaty of Nanjing (1842)' - consistent. Article's Jin dynasty lake date given as 282 (no CE marker in article; I added CE).

Article lead says founded around the 12th century and part of the Danish Kingdom in the 16th century, while the history section says founded by 1200 and gives 1460-1864 as its time as Denmark's second port; the text uses only 'by 1200'. Entry's plebiscite of 1920 and Dönitz arrest not in article.
Article gives Armistice death toll 1,400,000; left out. Article says second term from November 1917; entry 1917-1920, consistent.
Article gives two accounts of the 1155 coronation (Pavia 24 April or Monza 15 April); left out. Entry gives drowning 1190; consistent.

Entry says Ganja is Azerbaijan's second-largest city; article says third in its lead and second in its transport section: ranking left out. Article gives three foundation dates (859-60 Arabic history; 846-47 Armenian historian, 659-60 Mustawfi): only the first printed. Entry says Ganja name restored 1918 and 1989; consistent. Left out 2020 attacks, 2016 Youth Capital, mayor.
Thin history in article; entry's 1871/1876 creation facts not in article and left out. Left out population, GDP, crime, tourism, sports. Entry says 'was a centre of coal mining' not in article.
Article's Avvaiyar claim (3rd century BCE) is dubious; omitted. Entry type is idea.

Article's Hungarian-revolution section is partisan (Hungarian reading on revoking April laws); omitted. Maximilian is called 'Emperor Maximilian I of Mexico' in article. 'last veto by a Catholic ruler' = article's 'last use of such a veto'. Entry dates 'r. 1848-1916'; consistent.

Entry's Ludwig Railway fact is not in the article; left out. Entry says one of the largest Jewish communities in southern Germany: article only says 'Franconian Jerusalem'. Left out population, mayor, companies in detail.
Left out population, tourism figures, utilities, 2024 election.
Left out all census, election, GDP, congestion and ranking figures. Entry says created 1994; article says PWV 1994, renamed 1995.
No conflict with entry. Left out the article's modern commemoration details (post-2010).
Entry says the present shape dates from 1881; article does not say, so not printed. Left out lists of cities, transport, education, a 2010 dating website.
Thin article (467 words); text is below 260 words by necessity. Left out politics, tourism statistics, population figure for 2023, climate comparison of Auch.

Article lead gives war end 28 January 1871; armistice 26 January in section text; I wrote Paris fell 28 January and armistice agreed without giving its date. Desc says proclamation of German Empire at Versailles in January 1871; I wrote 'in the last days of the war' as the article does.
Desc says 'escaped in 1838' consistent. Did not name 'minister to Haiti' (in desc, not in article excerpt).

Entry says founded as Anglo-Norman town by the de Burghs in 13th century; article says Dún Gaillimhe fort completed 1124 by Tairrdelbach Ua Conchobair. I left out the 1124 founding and stated only the 1230s capture by de Burgh; the entry itself is arguably wrong/incomplete (an earlier fort existed). Left out transport, economy, politics, current officials, 2020 Capital of Culture.
Article says born in Smyrna; entry says near Smyrna: birthplace left unnamed. Ambassador to UK given as 1957-1962 in lead and 1957-1961 in biography: dates left out.
Section headings: the Jangal paragraph sits under 'The place today' for lack of a better heading from the list; editor may move. Left out demographics tables, universities, notable people.
Entry says Hanover raised from electorate in 1814 and governed through viceroy: not in the given text, not printed.
Entry's Hattin 1187 and Ain Jalut 1260 are not in the supplied text; not printed. Left out modern conflict (1970s-80s Lebanon operations), demographics, Judaization remark, cuisine.

SKIPPED: too little lasting material: the article is mostly current politics, officeholders and statistics, and the rest repeats the entry Article gives 65 municipalities in the lead and 63 in its list; not used.

Entry says proclaimed by his troops; article says the Senate proclaimed him after Nymphidius's false announcement: left the proclaimer unnamed. Article: 'Galba was murdered on the orders of Otho' in lead; body says conspiracy by Otho. Dates for his career are given by the article as approximate.
Article says Convention sent him to Leuven on 20 March 1793, and also lists the Revolutionary Tribunal on 10 March; order of paragraph events slightly unchronological but dates correct.
Entry says landed at Kagoshima and Otomo Sorin: not in article, not printed.
Birth: article says probably 1475, lead c. 1478, entry c. 1478: only 'the 1470s' printed. Left out statue history.
Entry says Futurists campaigned for Italy's entry into WWI: not in the supplied text, not printed. Left out dance, photography, lists of people, modern film echoes.
Entry says seat of the European Commission of the Danube (1856) and grain free port: not in the supplied text, not printed. Left out 2026 drone strike, floods, twin towns, neighbourhoods.
Article gives birth as 30 October / 9 November 1683; not printed. Entry's Dettingen 1743 not in the text, only the battle's name.
Article gives Lingotto built 1915-1918 in one place and begun 1922, opened 1923 in another: no dates printed. Left out current model lists, leadership list, marketing, current CEO.

Entry says Shelley aged 18 conceived it; article gives 18 for 1816 and says 20 at publication: fine. Lead says she started writing in Bath at 18; not printed. Left out the Frankenstein name's origins debates and modern adaptations.
Article gives presidencies 1940-44, 1952-54, 1955-59; not repeated. Left out the dispute over Bohemia magazine's 20,000 figure.
SKIPPED: article under about 250 words of history; mostly census, climate and transport; nothing on founding beyond the entry (capital date 1970 not in article)
Entry says founded 1785 by Loyalists, chosen by Governor Thomas Carleton, UNB 1785; article says 1783 arrival, 1784 renaming, King's College undated. Left out founding year, Carleton and UNB date.

Article gives opening date 20 May per Socrates 'though it may have been later in June'; left out. Wrote Constantine's successors as 'ruled the east after him' (Constantius II son, Valens) per article.
Left out film adaptation lists.
Entry says elector of Hanover from 1698; article says ruler from 1698, ratified prince-elector 1708; wrote 'his territories'. Entry's Bremen and Verden and privy council not in article.
Entry says a stanza of A Toast is the anthem; article says Zdravljica declared anthem in 1989; followed article.
Politics section omitted.
Entry says arrested 1639 under Olivares; article gives arrest without naming cause. Date of La cuna y la sepultura differs inside article; omitted.
Entry's Aquitani/Gauls boundary not in article; not used.
Article gives presidency 1930-1945 and 1951-54 consistent with entry.
Consistent with entry.
Entry's Concordat of Fontainebleau 1813 and UNESCO status not in article; entry says Napoleon signed abdication in the palace, article gives only farewell and treaty.
Article mentions still lifes only in lead.

Article gives first empire ending 1814, entry 'largely lost by 1815'; no end year written. Entry says first empire built from seventeenth century; article's sixteenth-century attempts written as failures.
Entry says renamed Prince of Wales Island; not in article.
Article cites Guinness record 'since 1625'; wrote 'often said'.
Entry says Tusculum refugees 'said to have settled'; article says village existed by 9th century and population increased after 1191; written as increased.
Article's account of his affair omitted deliberately. Entry's baldacchino, Four Rivers fountain and Ecstasy of Saint Teresa: Four Rivers appears only in a list in the article; not used.
Entry says Nobunaga captured it in 1567; article gives no date. Wrote 'followed Dōsan in the castle'.

Article gives several casualty totals; both Riehn and Zamoyski quoted and attributed. Article says Napoleon 'lost more than 500,000 of 615,000' too; left out. Entry says Napoleon's retreat in winter destroyed most of army; article says losses were greatest in summer/autumn, so text only says snow and frost followed and cites the dispute over the saying.

Entry says he crushed Spartacist uprising and defended republic against Kapp Putsch and 1923 crisis; article only mentions Kapp Putsch in lead, so those events not detailed. Entry says first President in February 1919 (provisional); article agrees.

Entry says 'mainly over control of Korea'; consistent. Article gives Chinese troop figures 2,700-2,800 (lead) and 2,465 (timeline) and 3,000-3,500 by July; text gives the range 2,465 to 2,800. Article says Korea proclaimed itself Korean Empire in 1892 (probably a slip, 1897); left out. Article lead says Qing sued for peace in February 1895 and treaty two months later; consistent.

Entry says Trinci ruled from 1305 until papacy took it in 1439; article gives no 1305 and says the Palazzo Governativo passed to the municipality in 1439. Text avoids stating when Trinci rule began or ended. Article gives Saint Felician martyred 251 - omitted. Article lead says 'ancient town'.

Article states Papen convinced Schuschnigg to sign away sovereignty on 12 Feb 1938, while also saying the tribunal found no solid evidence of involvement in the annexation; the Schuschnigg claim left out. Article lead says Vice-Chancellor 1933 to 1934, consistent with the text. Hitler appointed 30 January is NOT in the wp file explicitly (it says Hindenburg formally gave Papen the task on 28 January); check flagged if any.

Entry says isolated insulin in 1921 to 1922 and died in air crash in 1941; consistent. Article's own text gives first insulin injection 11 January 1922. Article lead calls him pharmacologist, orthopedist and field surgeon.

Entry says Pius IX took refuge 1848-1850; article says November 1848 to 4 September 1849. Text omits the dates. Article mentions Gaeta 'stormed' 1707 etc, omitted. 'since 1967' for flagship base is a bare historical fact.

Article says British occupied Hong Kong after Chuenpi, 26 January 1841 flag raised. Article says Pottinger arrived 10 August (year not explicit in text; context is 1841). Article's timeline of Yangtze campaign 1842 implied (Treaty 1842). Gladstone quote paraphrased.
